subject: Activation contingency & minimum GPU anchors for HelioThera deal
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@heliothera.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Aug 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated options—activation contingency + min GPU anchors

Hi Alyssa,

Following up from our onboarding call last week — attached is a short options sheet with three dedicated reservation constructs for HelioThera. I pulled these to align to the traffic profiles you shared (inbound clinical inference + nightly batch retraining), and to give you an explicit ramp/contingency path so procurement can model cost and risk.

Quick summary (see attached helio_dedicated_options_v1.xlsx for numbers):
- Option A — Anchored small: 24 GPUs (min guarantee 12) for 6 months, burstable to 36 for scheduled retrains. Fastest go-live, lowest initial spend.
- Option B — Ramp ladder: Start 12 GPUs (min guarantee 8) then add 8 GPUs/month to reach 40 by month 6, with a 2-month credit window for missed throughput.
- Option C — Stabilized slate: 48 GPUs with staged warm-starts and a 3-month pro-rata credit if latency SLOs miss during initial activation.

Two asks for procurement/engineering to confirm:
1) Is a hard minimum (billing floor) acceptable or do you need a soft floor with usage credits?
2) Is HelioThera comfortable with an activation window (we recommend 10 business days for full warm cache and throughput tests) or do you need a shorter SLA for production cutover?

I dropped an activation timeline PDF in the attachments. If helpful, Karthik can sketch a per-route GPU mapping (inference vs. retrain lanes) so you can see how the min guarantees translate to tail latency and concurrency.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwoodinference.com

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@heliothera.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated options—activation contingency + min GPU anchors

Thanks Naomi — good framing. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement will prefer a soft floor if we can get predictable unit economics via credits. Hard minimums trigger governance overhead with finance.
- Our primary requirement is 99th percentile inference latency <= 300ms for clinical routing (peak daytime). Nightly retrain jobs can be queued and stretched but we need a defined burst plan.
- We also want an explicit rollback/escape hatch in month 2 if model accuracy/regression occurs.

Can Karthik share a mapping of how Option B would look if we frontload GPUs for day-one critical routes (i.e., prioritize concurrency across three inference endpoints) versus spreading evenly? That will help us evaluate immediate risk.

Also looping in Liam (ops) and Procurement.

Best,
Alyssa
VP Product, HelioThera
alyssa@heliothera.ai

Hi Alyssa — quick technical sketch below for Option B with the two variants you asked for. I kept the math conservative to preserve latency SLOs while minimizing early spend.

Variant 1 — Frontload critical routes (fast day-one latency for three endpoints):
- Day 0: Provision 28 GPUs (min guarantee 20).
- Distribution: 18 GPUs for inference lanes (split across 3 endpoints for headroom), 10 GPUs reserved for scheduled retrains / KV cache population.
- Expected 99p latency: ~220–280ms depending on sequence length and batching policy.
- Ramp: add 6 GPUs at week 3 and month 2 to reach 40 by month 2.
- Contingency: soft floor credits equal to 20% of monthly committed spend if utilization < 45% for any 30-day window.

Variant 2 — Even spread (lower day-one spend, gradual risk exposure):
- Day 0: Provision 12 GPUs (min guarantee 8).
- Distribution: 8 GPUs for inference, 4 GPUs for retrain-batching/eviction.
- Expected 99p latency: ~300–380ms during peak until month 3 when additional GPUs come online.
- Ramp: add 8 GPUs/month to reach 40 by month 6.
- Contingency: ability to burst to 60 GPUs for scheduled retrains (pre-booked windows) with overage pricing; finance credits only apply after month 4 if SLOs are missed more than twice.

Notes on warm-start & cache priming:
- Full warm KV cache for critical routes requires ~7–10 days of synthetic replay and live traffic to hit stable tail performance; the activation window Naomi mentioned covers this.
- We recommend pre-populating prefixes for the top 10 clinical flows to reduce cold-start variance.

Next steps I propose: pick the variant you prefer and we’ll convert to a commercial term (soft-floor credit %, burst pricing, DocuSign-ready activation clause). Marissa can lead the commercial draft.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[karthik@redwoodinference.com]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Aug 2028 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated options—activation contingency + min GPU anchors

Alyssa / Liam — thanks for the signal. Based on the team preference on the call and Karthik’s sketch, here’s the recommended deal path we’ll put in the formal proposal:

Agreed path (to include in SOW / Term Sheet):
- Start with Variant 1 (frontloaded): 28 GPUs provisioned Day 0, billing floor 20 GPUs (soft floor via credits at 20% monthly spend if utilization < 45%).
- Ramp: add 6 GPUs at week 3 and add remaining 6 GPUs at day-60 to reach 40 GPUs by month 2.
- Activation window: 10 business days for warm-starting and throughput validation; we’ll run an agreed replay and synthetic test plan during that window.
- Escape hatch: 30-day rollback clause in month 2 if accuracy regressions occur (refund of pro-rated committed fees for month 2 if regression verification passes).
- Burst: pre-bookable burst to 60 GPUs for retrain windows; overage pricing at the agreed uplift (see attached pricing appendix).

Action items:
- HelioThera: confirm acceptance of soft floor + escape hatch (reply with thumbs-up or comments by Wed 22 Aug).
- Naomi/Marissa: we’ll convert to a term sheet and share a DocuSign by EOD Thu 23 Aug.
- Karthik: include the top-10 prefix priming checklist for the activation playbook in the SOW.

If we get buy-in on the soft-floor language, procurement can sign faster and we’ll schedule a week-0 activation runbook workshop.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
